A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with directly matching methods, equations and main experiments. v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–8 that are absent from the supplied v3; this is an observable omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, sensitivity and repeatability experiments, plus a live-device demonstration in supplementary Section 8.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results on MPIIGaze, EVE and GazeCapture, including the comparisons, ablations and repeatability analysis in Section 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same differentiable projection, dynamic pseudo-labeling with transformation T, SVD alignment and color-jitter loss. Omitted supplementary implementation details do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The three evaluation datasets and Gaze360 pretraining remain unchanged. v3 omits the additional live desktop-webcam scenario involving a volunteer tracking a moving dot, narrowing the reported evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged, including EFE, IVGaze and the adaptation baselines. RAT remains plotted in Figure 4 and discussed in Section 4.4 despite removal of its caption sentence.

E3.justification: The retained benchmark protocols, preprocessing, training budgets and metrics are unchanged. v3 omits the separate live-test protocol: four calibration points with 40 images each, a webcam approximately 90 cm away, and moving-dot evaluation without post-processing.

E4.justification: The live-device case study in v1’s supplementary Section 8 and Figures 8–9 is absent from v3. Component ablations, alternative adaptation strategies, sample-count sensitivity, repeatability and pseudo-label trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten trials using different MPIIGaze training samples, evaluated across 15 subjects, with interquartile boxes, full-range whiskers, means and medians in Figure 6. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The qualitative live-device trajectory result in Figure 9 is omitted. Main results remain unchanged: Table 2 reports 43.4, 56.7 and 35.7 mm for EVE, MPIIGaze and GazeCapture, respectively, and the repeatability average remains 55.6 mm.

T1.justification: The task definition, projection and inverse-projection derivations, alignment formulation and losses in Equations 1–12 are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about cross-task few-shot adaptation, source-free and screen-calibration-free operation, the proposed components and benchmark advantages.

C2.justification: v3 loses supplementary discussion connecting GazeCapture’s manual geometric measurements to screen calibration, and attributing live-test jitter to blinking and unstable face detection with suggested post-processing remedies. The main projection-failure limitations and interpretation of the GazeCapture ablation remain.

D1.justification: The omitted supplement removes reproducibility information spanning identifier-ordered subject selection, dataset statistics, estimated camera intrinsics, PyTorch3D usage, initial rotation R = diag(-1, 1, -1), and the live-device pipeline. Core training hyperparameters remain, but references to the missing supplement persist. The project-page address also changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gudi, Li and van Gemert’s Efficiency in real-time webcam gaze tracking to Section 2.1 and the references. The remaining research positioning is unchanged; this addition is not an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: v3 updates author and affiliation information, identifies a corresponding author, adds acknowledgments and shortens the Figure 4 caption and Section 4.7 ending. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged, while the supplementary sections are omitted.

P2.justification: v3 omits dataset Table 6, device photograph Figure 8 and trajectory Figure 9. Main Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–7 retain their displays, with limited caption and surrounding text-reflow changes.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the core method, benchmark evidence and main limitations, but loses supplementary sampling and initialization details and the live-device demonstration. This weakens reproducibility and support for practical applicability. The limited citation and editorial updates provide little compensation, yielding a limited overall quality decline.
